/projects/omega-platform.title: Project Details – Product Designer
h6: Skills: Figma, UI/UX, Prototyping, Jira, Desktop layout, User Journey Mapping, Design Systems, Mantine UI, Miro
p: The most significant challenge in developing the Omega Platform was ensuring the coherence and consistency of the projects created. To achieve this, we employed a proprietary design system called Megawatt, which was specifically designed to establish a robust visual identity while maintaining a modern and exclusive aesthetic. Throughout the project, I had the opportunity to work across various resolutions, including PC, Tablet, and Mobile devices. Additionally, I engaged in prototyping, which played a crucial role in providing the developers with a clear understanding of the intended design and functionality. One of the key challenges we faced was minimizing the use of modals, streamlining the application’s design, and optimizing the website’s performance. Furthermore, I contributed to the development of new components, such as icons, grids, and inputs, which were seamlessly integrated into the design system.

The Megawatt was meticulously crafted from the ground up to replace the outdated design system, granting us the freedom to create components and diverse styles. Throughout this project, we engaged in numerous feedback sessions and testing sessions. I collaborated closely with the developers and users of the platform to identify areas for improvement. During my time working on the new website, I also participated in design sessions with the other product designers on the team. Our objective was to ensure that the project was user-friendly and easy to build. I leveraged my front-end skills to ensure that all implemented features were feasible. Once we had clearly defined our goals, we commenced the project using Mantine UI. We organized the deliveries into Minimum Viable Products (MVPs). The most critical features were prioritized for development, enabling users to provide feedback and optimize their workflows.

Beyond Brazil, it has begun international expansion with a wind park in Texas, USA. Its strategy emphasizes sustainability, affordable access to renewable energy, and positive social impact.

/projects/credit-portability-bradesco.title: Project Details – Product Designer
h6: Skills: Figma, UI/UX, UX Writing, Prototyping, Animations, Mobile layout, User Journey Mapping, Design Systems, Accessibility, Wireframes
p: The credit portability process permits a customer to transfer a credit agreement from one financial institution to another through Open Banking, enabling better payment terms and lower fees.
This is a complex project due to the set of rules that this process must follow, including issues involving deadlines, cancellations, banking agreements, and debt repayment between banks.
Furthermore, the launch of this feature was required to meet a deadline defined by the Central Bank.

From the outset, we established a pre-defined structure for the project. On the client side, it was divided into two distinct categories: customers who had already granted Open Banking permissions and those who had not.

From the bank’s perspective, we had to create a “defense” journey. This meant that banks receiving requests for portability to another bank could defend themselves by submitting a new proposal to the client within a three-day timeframe.
We were left with three distinct journeys to develop, each with its own unique characteristics. We submitted the prototype for research, where we gathered valuable user feedback.

Bradesco is Brazil’s third-largest private bank, founded in 1943. It offers retail and corporate banking, asset management, and insurance, with a strong nationwide presence. The bank has been key to expanding financial inclusion and remains a major player in Brazil’s economic and financial development.

/projects/cashback-app-project.title: Project Details – Product Designer
h6: Skills: Figma, UI/UX, Prototyping, Notion, Desktop and Mobile layouts, Design Systems, Chakra UI, AI Generated Images, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator
p: This was a freelance project that I worked on for seven months. The task was to design the user interface (UI) of a cashback app with user-friendly features and an appealing design.
Since I was the sole designer on this project, I had complete control over all the UI/UX decisions.

Before I started, they told me they were having trouble getting started because the project scope was still very raw. I sat down with everyone involved and tried to understand the nature of the project and where they intended to go.

My first step here was to understand the scope, the competition, and the basic features of the project. Benchmarking and priority mapping were necessary. Also, we organized a workflow, and I began creating the user journey and user interface.

This project had numerous feedback sessions, even during the building phase. We had very short deadlines, so I had to ensure that we could achieve a good result without slowing down. Creating the entire UI library from scratch was extremely helpful.

I had to be two steps ahead of the developers, and I kept my pace really nicely. They always had some work to do, and in the meantime, I could make improvements in other parts of the project. My last task was to create an admin panel. The P.O. was very pleased with the result.

/projects/sigma-gd-serena.title: Project Details – Product Designer
h6: Skills: Figma, UI/UX, Prototyping, Jira, Desktop layout, User Journey Mapping, Design Systems, Mantine UI, Miro
p: SIGMA GD is a crucial project for Serena Energia. The GD in its name stands for distributed generation, a business model Serena was unfamiliar with until 2023. In essence, they primarily engaged in B2B businesses, while GD (DG) focused on B2C.

Consequently, they lacked a solution to manage GD clients, which prompted us to embark on this project. The project involved handling data of thousands of clients, with the primary criterion being to prioritize those who required more attention. I dedicated two years to this project.

Our challenge here was to create an entire solution for a very particular problem. There weren't a lot of client and billing management applications that could take into account the particularities of the energy market. We had just one known app to take inspiration from.

The solution had to be robust enough to handle thousands of clients, with expectations to grow to millions. We utilized a free and scalable UI Library and adapted it to our needs. The requirements were meticulously mapped, and the user flows created.

Once we had our goals defined, we commenced the project using Mantine UI. We organized the deliveries into MVPs. The most crucial features were prioritized for development, allowing users to provide feedback and optimize their workflows.

After two years, the app was capable of importing customers' bills through APIs, generating reports, and sending Serena's bills for payment. It was also capable of reacting to energy tariff changes and adapting to them. The result was a very complete application.

/projects/amortization-bradesco.title: Project Details – Product Designer
h6: Skills: Figma, UI/UX, UX Writing, Prototyping, Animations, Mobile layout, User Journey Mapping, Design Systems, Accessibility, Wireframes
p: This project was divided into a two-phase MVP, and it’s particularly challenging. The objective is to digitize the process of requesting an amortization from your credit contract, as the name implies.

However, the bank responsible for handling Severance Pay Funds is a government-linked institution. If you’re unfamiliar with severance pay funds, they’re reserves set aside for employees after a specified period of employment.
Consequently, we encountered significant bureaucratic hurdles and had to ensure the accuracy of the information we handled, as it involved clients’ money.

The initial MVP aimed to allow clients to submit documents through the app instead of visiting an agency and speaking with a manager, a process that remains prevalent today. The challenge was that clients had to fill out a large PDF. The second MVP is expected to eliminate the need for the PDF entirely by providing a user-friendly and guided journey.

After defining the project’s approach in the initial phases, I created some wireframes. Following an initial presentation with stakeholders, my coworkers and I began working on high-fidelity prototypes. With said prototypes in hand, we conducted user research and gathered feedback from clients, which informed our subsequent refinement of the journey.

Although the user only needs to fill out a form and submit documents, this process requires significant attention from them. Additionally, we must present a substantial amount of information throughout the journey to prevent request denials. Our initial prototype performed exceptionally well, but some clients found it still lacking clarity. To address this, we collaborated with the research team and other designers to refine the prototypes based on their insights and perspectives.

The refined prototypes received exceptional feedback from leadership and stakeholders. After validations, thorough inspections, and final adjustments, we finally shipped it to development. In March 2026, this project will be available to over 109 million clients, significantly optimizing an outdated process that could take up to 3 months to just 10 days.
